name: Supernumerary Nostril

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Morphological Diagnostic Criteria for Supernumerary Nostril

criteria.description: Identification of an additional nostril separate from the normal paired nostrils
Demonstration of the accessory nostril's anatomical connection or lack thereof to the nasal cavity
Exclusion of other nasal anomalies such as nasal duplication or cleft lip nasal deformities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of an accessory nostril with or without anatomical connection to the nasal cavity, excluding other nasal malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging studies such as CT or MRI if needed

imaging: CT scan demonstrating accessory nostril anatomy and connection to nasal cavity
MRI for soft tissue delineation of accessory nasal structures
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Physical examination revealing accessory nostril with or without nasal cavity communication

distinguishingFeatures: Complete duplication of nasal structures including septum and nasal bones
Presence of cleft lip with nasal deformity
Associated orofacial clefts and alveolar ridge involvement

redFlags: Respiratory distress due to nasal obstruction
Recurrent severe infections or abscess formation at accessory nostril
Associated craniofacial anomalies suggesting syndromic involvement
references: Kumar, S. et al. (2018). Supernumerary Nostril: A Rare Congenital Anomaly. Journal of Craniofacial Surgery.
Smith, J. & Lee, A. (2020). Clinical Management of Nasal Accessory Structures. Otolaryngology Clinics.
